subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: What default and fail-soft boundary should OpenClaw use when Docker sandbox prep is slow or unresponsive, and should the fix cover only Docker exec/init or the full prune/layout/config-hash/backend prep path?
rationale: The source gap is real, but timeout defaults and fail-soft sandbox availability can intentionally turn slow Docker hosts into runtime failures, and the issue names multiple possible slow substeps.

options.title: Refresh full prep fix
options.body: Require a refreshed or replacement PR that bounds the whole sandbox prep control-plane path, preserves current workspace behavior, documents any config/default surface, and includes real Docker or OrbStack proof.

options.title: Land narrow Docker mitigation
options.body: Accept a narrower Docker exec/init timeout as an interim mitigation while explicitly tracking prune, layout, and config-hash waits as follow-up work.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter or maintainer can isolate the exact slow substep from attached logs or a live macOS/OrbStack reproduction.

recommendation.title: Refresh full prep fix
recommendation.body: Require a refreshed or replacement PR that bounds the whole sandbox prep control-plane path, preserves current workspace behavior, documents any config/default surface, and includes real Docker or OrbStack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame ties the central Docker exec and sandbox context implementation to vincentkoc, making them the best available owner for the immediate code-path decision.
